labels.label: def:portly_skeletal_subset

hypotheses.paper: X Hausdorff, locally connected (ambient of the definition)
hypotheses.note: the predicates take no hypothesis; each theorem carries the classes it uses

questions: l.362 'W ∩ U is connected': read with IsPreconnected (empty set allowed). For open dense U it is equivalent to the IsConnected reading (GX.isLocallyConnectedIn_iff_isConnected), so IsPortly is unaffected; the reading only matters for 'locally connected in X' applied to non-dense sets.

labels.label: ex:following_example_skeletal_itemize

hypotheses.paper: item 1: S finite, X a surface
hypotheses.note: proved for S closed countable in any space charted on a real normed space of dimension > 1 (no Hausdorff needed there); the surface corollary assumes T2 only to get S closed

hypotheses.paper: item 2: S a tame knot in a 3-manifold
hypotheses.note: reading: closed locally flat subset (flat charts onto open subsets of R x R^2 sending S to R x {0}); general codimension >= 2 version GX.isSkeletal_of_locallyFlat needs only X locally connected

hypotheses.paper: item 3: k-skeleton of a pure n-dim simplicial complex, k <= n-2
hypotheses.note: false as written; corrected form adds local strong connectivity in codimension >= 2 (GX.IsLocallyStronglyConnected) and finiteness of K

hypotheses.paper: item 4: a Cantor wildly embedded in an n-manifold
hypotheses.note: any closed totally disconnected subset, any embedding, finite-dimensional model of dimension >= 2

sorries.obstruction: dimension theory: a closed totally disconnected subset of R^n is zero-dimensional and a subset of dimension <= n-2 does not separate R^n (Hurewicz-Wallman Thm IV 4 / Alexander duality / Borsuk separation). Not in mathlib; mathlib's countable-complement argument does not reach uncountable K, and straight-line general position fails (a Cantor set can meet every ray from a point). Everything else of item 4 (chart localisation, transfer of total disconnectedness through univBall, density) is proved.

local structure theory of geometric simplicial complexes, absent from mathlib (carrier of a point, open stars as a neighbourhood basis of K.space, star of a point as the cone on its link, connectedness of an open simplex with its open codimension-one faces, and the general-position step that a path avoiding the (n-2)-skeleton crosses facets only through open (n-1)-faces). The reduction k < n-2 to k = n-2 is proved (GX.isSkeletal_skeletonSpace).

findings: Item 3 (l.372) is false as written: the bow-tie (two closed triangles of R^2 sharing only the vertex 0) is a finite pure 2-dimensional simplicial complex whose 0-skeleton is not skeletal: a small open star of 0 is connected, removing 0 disconnects it (GX.bowtie_counterexample, built as a mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex). The item needs local strong connectivity in codimension >= 2 (every two n-simplices containing a simplex of dimension <= n-2 are joined through (n-1)-faces containing it), as for normal pseudomanifolds; the bow-tie fails exactly this (GX.not_isLocallyStronglyConnected_bowtie). The same caveat applies to l.625 ('gluings of projective polyhedra ... complement of the (n-2)-skeleton ... skeletal'), which is true for gluings that are pseudomanifolds but not for arbitrary face gluings.

Item 4 (l.373) needs n >= 2: in R no nonempty subset is skeletal (GX.eq_empty_of_isSkeletal_real), so a Cantor set in a 1-manifold is not skeletal. 'Wildly' presupposes n >= 3 anyway, so this is a precision rather than an error; the statement holds for tame and wild embeddings alike.

The closure properties l.383-390 never use Hausdorff; the two map items (l.389, l.390) need only the SOURCE locally connected; 'U portly in X, U ⊆ V implies U portly in V' (l.385) holds for an arbitrary subset V, not only open ones, when X is locally connected.
questions: 'surface' read as a Hausdorff space charted on R^2 (no second countability, no smoothness).
'tame knot' read as a closed locally flat subset (charts onto open subsets of R x R^2 sending the knot to R x {0}); the circle structure is unused.
'Cantor wildly embedded' read as a closed totally disconnected subset (compactness and perfectness unused).

'pure n-dimensional simplicial complex' read as a finite geometric complex (mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex) in a finite-dimensional real normed space with the subspace topology; pure = every face has <= n+1 vertices and lies in a face with n+1 vertices.

hypotheses.note: not used: the path lemma is applied in its relative form inside a connected open V

hypotheses.paper: X first countable, locally path-connected, Hausdorff
hypotheses.note: Hausdorff used only for the Hausdorff conclusion

kb_proposals: Portly API lives in GXScaffold/Topology/Portly.lean: the workhorse is GX.isPreconnected_of_local (a dense subset of a preconnected W is preconnected if it is locally preconnected); every closure property and every example reduces to it.

To show a closed S is skeletal, use GX.isSkeletal_of_local, and in a chart GX.exists_nhds_of_chart reduces it to small balls around e x; OpenPartialHomeomorph.univBall turns 'ball minus T' into 'E minus preimage of T'.

Infinite concatenation of paths: GX.Path.exists_infConcat (paths phi n : c n ~> c (n+1) shrinking to b give a path c 0 ~> b); built on ℝ by floor + Path.extend and LocallyFinite.continuousOn_iUnion, then reparametrised by t/(1-t).

At this pin symm_image_image_of_subset_source is stated on PartialEquiv: for an OpenPartialHomeomorph use e.toPartialEquiv.symm_image_image_of_subset_source via Eq.trans (rw does not see through the coercion).

Affine independence of a Finset's vertices in a Geometry.SimplicialComplex: state it as AffineIndependent ℝ (Subtype.val : ↥(s : Set E) → E); the ((↑) : (s : Set E) → E) spelling fails to elaborate. For three points go through affineIndependent_iff_not_collinear_set and h.range.

A def quantifying over Finset intersections (IsLocallyStronglyConnected) must take [DecidableEq E], not open Classical: otherwise the instance differs from instDecidableEqProd at use sites and terms do not unify.
notes: Two tagged sorries, both in ex:following_example_skeletal_itemize and both on theories absent from mathlib (dimension theory for item 4; local structure of geometric simplicial complexes for corrected item 3). Every other declaration is sorry-free (#print axioms checked for path_covering, portly_first_countable, bowtie_counterexample, isSkeletal_of_tameKnot, isSkeletal_of_finite_surface, isPortly_iUnion_of_local, IsPortly.image_of_isOpenMap).
